analysis.title: Global Economics Analyst: Macro Outlook 2027: Steady Baseline, Downside Risks
key_insights: Global GDP grew 2.7% in 2026, in line with potential and 0.1pp below GS's 2026 outlook projection. Surging AI capex, easier financial conditions and fiscal expansion (US, Germany, parts of Asia) mostly offset the energy supply shock from the Iran war.
Global headline inflation is on course to end 2026 at 3.7% Q4/Q4, 1.3pp above GS's forecast from last year, because of the Iran war.

GS forecasts 2.8% global GDP growth in 2027, 0.1pp above potential. US is 2.4% vs 2.2% consensus, Euro area 0.9% vs 1.3% consensus, China 4.5% vs 4.4% consensus, South Korea 3.2% vs 2.7%, Taiwan 6.3% vs 5.9%.

Energy flips from a 0.4pp drag on global growth in 2026 to a modest boost in 2027. The commodity baseline has Brent falling to $78/bbl by end-2027 as Middle East supply adapts, with LNG prices normalizing similarly. Europe keeps a drag from delayed energy cost pass-through.

The GS FCI has tightened about 50bp in the US and 30bp in DMs over three months on lower equity prices and higher rates, implying a moderate growth drag over the next few quarters. The DM fiscal impulse turns only slightly positive: Japan adds 0.7pp to GDP growth, Germany and the US are modestly positive, and the UK stays a drag. The US positive reflects expected reversal of some 2025 OBBBA spending cuts after the Democratic win in November's election.

Global nominal AI investment is forecast to rise from $1.1tn in 2026 to $1.8tn in 2027, driven by over $500bn more US hardware spending. The year-over-year change as a share of GDP peaks in 2027H1 and the level peaks in 2028. AI adds 0.4pp to global growth, and 0.2pp to measured US growth (0.6pp 'true' growth after correcting for undercounted chip investment and IP exports).

China is a modest 0.1pp headwind to rest-of-world growth in 2027, with larger drags in Germany (-0.3pp) and Central Europe (-0.2pp). The cause is strong Chinese exports and a wider trade surplus against weak domestic demand, with a 1.3pp of GDP property drag.

Downside risk 1 is a renewed Iran escalation. The commodity team's upside scenario (shipping attacks, infrastructure damage, persistent risk premium) takes oil to $132/bbl, and FCI and fiscal impulses would not offset it in 2027 as they did in 2026.

Downside risk 2 is bond market turbulence. The DM yield curve is 85bp above its early-2026 level, which if sustained would subtract a cumulative 0.5% from GDP via housing, consumer durables and business investment. Only part of this drag is in the baseline because GS expects fewer hikes than priced.

France is the acute fiscal risk. The 10-year OAT trades about 150bp over bunds, and GS expects no meaningful consolidation before the April 2027 presidential and June 2027 parliamentary elections (0.8pp deficit cut forecast for 2028). Fiscal indicators are 'flashing red', so markets could force earlier consolidation.

Downside risk 3 is a weaker AI impulse. Hyperscaler equity reactions to capex signals turned slightly negative in 2026 after being positive in 2024-2025, and upward capex revisions slowed in the Q3 earnings season. The labor-market transition is backloaded to 2028-2029, when US productivity trend rises to 2.5-3% and unemployment drifts to 4.5%.

Additional AI investment risks: capacity constraints (semiconductor and memory backlogs through 2028, which could raise prices without raising real output), credit markets ($687bn AI-related debt and $115bn equity issued in 2026, with more crowd-out of other investment possible in 2027) and regulation (data center permitting moratoria in states such as Texas after the early-November midterms). GS does not expect regulation to derail 2027 investment because permits are mostly issued.

AI is starting to show in the labor market. Across non-manufacturing industries, firm AI adoption now has a statistically significant negative correlation with employment growth (t-stat -2.53) and positive correlation with unemployment (t-stat 4.13), both insignificant at the start of the year. GS still sees the effect as temporary, about +0.5pp on unemployment over several years, and expects displacement to accelerate in a downturn.

Inflation should slow in 2027. Tariff pass-through (still adding 40bp to y/y core PCE through October) drops out by next spring and the Iran energy impulse fades. GS expects US core PCE to fall from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% at end-2027.

Near-term inflation upside risks: remaining energy pass-through (especially European airfares), higher memory prices from AI demand (the US weights software and accessories too heavily, exaggerating the effect), broadening upstream cost pressures, and a US 'January effect' (forecast includes a 0.1pp boost to January core PCE). Wage growth and shelter inflation are trending down and ease the core services risk.
In the Iran escalation scenario, GS rules of thumb imply 0.9pp upside to 2027 headline inflation and 0.2pp to core versus baseline.

Fed: GS expects hikes in December and March, one cut in December 2027, then three cuts in 2028 to a 3.25-3.5% terminal rate. Scenario weights are 50% baseline, 35% four hikes with a higher terminal rate and 15% recession. US risks skew more dovish than elsewhere because inflation drivers look more temporary and the US is most exposed to an AI downturn.

ECB: final hike in December (another in Q1 possible), then cuts toward a 2.25% terminal rate starting 2027Q4. BoE: final hike to 4.25% in February, hold through 2027, cuts to 3.25% from 2028. BoC: two hikes to 3.0% in 1H27, likely to underdeliver versus market pricing, with the neutral range revised to 2.5-3.5% in April. RBA: hold at 4.85% through October, 125bp of cuts by end-2028. BoJ is the outlier: hikes in December, March and June to a 2.0% terminal rate, with core CPI above 3.5% through next summer.

EM rates skew dovish. CEEMEA and LatAm central banks are expected to cut through 2027, and Asia flat to slightly higher with GS below market pricing except Taiwan. GS thinks markets overestimate EM inflation risk because inflation was low before the shock, EM economies are cyclically weak and EM currencies have held up.

Market baseline is positive returns in equities and bonds in 2027 and near-zero commodities. GS targets S&P 500 at 8,300 (3m), 8,500 (6m) and 8,700 (12m) versus 7,619 current. S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027.

The AI investment peak is a bigger test for markets than for the economy. AI contributed much more to earnings, market value and capex than to GDP, S&P 500 earnings are at a record high relative to GDP, and growth-rate peaks ('second derivative') often end the period of positive surprises. AI-infrastructure names have derated significantly since June.

Market risk is that the flattening and rotation away from AI winners becomes an aggregate shock, for example if the market looks ahead to the 2028 investment-share peak, the rotation to other sectors is slow, a fresh energy spike hits non-AI areas, or financial and credit feedback loops accelerate. GS sees the market risk as higher than the economic risk.

Rates and bonds: GS sees the US 10-year at 4.6% at end-2027 (4.99% now) and expects front-end pricing to fall further. Bonds failed to hedge equities in 2026, but as 2027 progresses risks shift toward growth and lower rates, with real yields the highest in many years, so bonds regain hedging value.
Credit: GS expects wider spreads in 2027 on heavier corporate supply, with US HY to underperform (USD HY 320bp to 410bp in 12m, USD IG 88bp to 105bp). Europe has more room to tighten than the US.
Regional equity allocation: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex-Japan/EM, underweight Europe.

FX and commodities: modest USD weakness (EUR/USD 1.11 to 1.15, USD/JPY 160 to 150, USD/CNY 6.66 to 6.30) with CNY appreciating on the trade surplus. The JPY would appreciate sharply in a growth-scare scenario. Commodities are valued as a hedge against oil spikes: WTI 86.5 to 70 and Brent 92.8 to 78 over 12m, with a variable oil risk premium above fundamentals.

Hedging ideas: positioning for lower rates in the US and Japan, or jointly lower rates and equities, USD/JPY downside, European gas futures and TTF calls for energy upside, and out-of-the-money equity puts or longer-dated calls replacing equity holdings. Equity index volatility has risen a little, is unlikely to fall much and could rise if macro stress broadens, while the sharpest volatility so far is under the surface of the indices.

sector_views.rationale: Resilient investment and ongoing AI-driven earnings growth, with S&P 500 EPS growth of 11% in 2027 cushioning the AI capex peak.
Fiscal boost of 0.7pp to GDP growth, and Topix target of 4,500 in 12 months from 3,929.
GS expects weak European growth (0.9% vs 1.3% consensus) from tighter financial conditions and energy costs biting this winter.
Allocation is neutral after accounting for risks around the baseline.
Heavier corporate supply and AI financing needs push spreads wider, with risk of turbulence from weaker borrowers in the tail.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 36% in 2026 slowing to 11% in 2027 (GS forecast). S&P 500 earnings are at a record high relative to GDP.
Upward revisions to hyperscaler capex slowed in the Q3 2026 earnings season. Memory price forecasts were revised higher over the same season.

0.1pp above potential. Energy turns into a tailwind and AI capex stays strong, offsetting tighter financial conditions and fiscal fade.
1.3pp above GS's forecast from last year because of the Iran war energy shock.
Tariff effects drop out of y/y data by spring and the energy impulse fades, so inflation falls.

trade_ideas.description: Position for lower US and Japan rates, or jointly lower rates and equities, as a hedge against deeper downside growth tails
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth risks later in 2027 favor bonds, and the US is most exposed to an AI downturn.
trade_ideas.risk: Fresh energy shocks or stickier core inflation could push yields higher.

trade_ideas.description: Short USD/JPY as a hedge against rates and equities falling together
trade_ideas.rationale: USD/JPY generally performs well when rates and equities both fall, and GS sees JPY appreciating sharply in a growth scare.

trade_ideas.description: Buy European gas futures and TTF calls as asymmetric protection against an energy upside shock
trade_ideas.rationale: Risk of renewed Iran escalation and a variable oil risk premium.

trade_ideas.description: Buy out-of-the-money equity puts, or replace equity holdings with longer-dated call options
trade_ideas.rationale: A maturing cycle and rising risk of a bumpy AI-peak transition make deeper equity protection more valuable than usual.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US and Japan equities, neutral Asia ex-Japan/EM, underweight Europe
trade_ideas.rationale: US resilient investment and AI earnings, Japan fiscal boost, and Europe weak growth and tighter financial conditions.
trade_ideas.risk: Faster rotation away from AI winners or a fresh energy spike.

risk_factors: Renewed Iran escalation pushing oil to $132/bbl, adding 0.9pp to 2027 headline inflation and 0.2pp to core.
Bond market turbulence from large deficits and AI-linked borrowing, especially in France ahead of the 2027 elections.
AI capex disappointment from capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress or weaker demand.
AI-driven job displacement spreading beyond technology and accelerating in a downturn.
Persistent core inflation in early 2027 from energy pass-through, memory prices, upstream costs and a January effect.
Credit spread widening from heavy AI-related corporate issuance, with US HY most exposed.
A rotation away from AI winners becoming a larger aggregate market shock, with risk to markets above risk to the economy.
Black swan risks such as a major cybersecurity event.
charts_described: Exhibit 26 baseline table in the appendix: GS 12-month forecasts of S&P 500 at 8,700, US 10-year yield at 4.60%, Brent at $78, and USD/JPY at 150.
Exhibit 12 regression: unemployment rate = -1.9 + 0.07 * AI adoption (t-stat 4.13), and employment growth = -0.1 - 0.1 * AI adoption (t-stat -2.53).
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has risen a little, is unlikely to fall much and has scope to rise further if macro stresses broaden. Longer-dated options can offer useful portfolio protection.
The sharpest volatility so far has been under the surface of the major equity indices, with rotations and derating of AI-infrastructure names that could spill into index-level moves.

Hedges proposed: out-of-the-money equity puts or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options, positioning for lower US and Japan rates or jointly lower rates and equities, USD/JPY downside, and European gas futures and TTF calls for energy upside.
AI-levered equities have derated significantly since June, and hyperscaler equity reactions to capex signals turned slightly negative in 2026.
geopolitical: War in Iran: energy supply shock in 2026, with risk of renewed escalation (shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure, persistent risk premium) driving oil to $132/bbl in the upside scenario.
Middle East supply adaptation lowering energy prices in the GS baseline, and faster progress toward resolution as a downside tail for energy prices.
France's April 2027 presidential and June 2027 parliamentary elections as the trigger point for fiscal consolidation.
US tariffs: pass-through is ending, and trade uncertainty weighs on Canadian policy.

US midterm elections in early November raising data center permitting moratoria risk, particularly in Texas. A Democratic victory in November's election is expected to reverse some 2025 OBBBA spending cuts.
China's rising trade surplus and weak domestic demand as a drag on rest-of-world growth.
Japan's Takaichi administration investment plans and defense spending adding to fiscal stimulus.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment and earnings stay firmly positive in 2027 (S&P 500 EPS +11%), cushioning the derating of AI beneficiaries, and leadership may pass to hyperscalers, AI adopters or non-AI companies as crowd-out eases.
tension_points.bear_case: The peak in AI investment growth ends the period of positive surprises and the market looks ahead to the 2028 peak in the investment share, with record earnings relative to GDP at risk and financing needs pushing up the cost of capital.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further slowing of upward hyperscaler capex revisions, or AI capex failing to rise strongly in 2027, would break the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Real yields are the highest in many years, GS sees growth risks rising later in 2027, and bonds should deliver more than running yield with greater capital gain scope later in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: A fresh energy shock, stickier core inflation, hawkish central banks and heavy deficits plus AI borrowing could push yields higher, as bonds failed to hedge equities for much of 2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed Iran escalation pushing energy prices sharply higher in the coming months, or core inflation staying firm, would delay the bond hedge.

tension_points.theme: Fed and central bank policy path
tension_points.bull_case: GS expects fewer hikes than priced, with the Fed cutting in December 2027 and a terminal rate of 3.25-3.5%, which boosts both equities and bonds.
tension_points.bear_case: A four-hike scenario with a higher terminal rate (35% probability) is possible if inflation proves stickier, including a US January effect and upstream cost pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core inflation surprises through spring 2027 or a renewed oil spike would push the Fed toward the four-hike scenario.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI investment growth stays robust in 2027 so the peak should be manageable for the economy, but it is already a bigger test for markets.
theme_stances.evidence: the peak in the AI investment impulse should be a manageable event for the economy
